jobs.title: SAP Transformation Leader
jobs.description:
An opportunity for an experienced SAP leader to oversee complex enterprise technology transformation initiatives.

About the Company

Our client is an established organization undergoing significant technology and business transformation, with a focus on modernizing enterprise systems, improving operational efficiency, and supporting long-term growth.

Who You Are

You are an experienced SAP program leader with a proven track record of delivering large-scale ERP transformations. You combine strong technical knowledge with practical execution skills and are comfortable leading cross-functional teams, managing complex projects, and engaging senior stakeholders. You bring a collaborative yet decisive leadership style and understand what it takes to deliver successful enterprise implementations.

Your Impact

The SAP Program Director will provide leadership and oversight for a major enterprise systems transformation. The role involves coordinating multiple workstreams, managing implementation priorities, and ensuring effective delivery across business and technology functions. You will work closely with senior leadership, internal teams, and external partners to drive program execution and successful outcomes.

What Are We Looking For?

SAP Implementation Experience:
Demonstrated experience leading large-scale SAP implementations, including SAP S/4HANA.
Program Delivery Leadership:
Proven ability to manage complex, end-to-end ERP transformation programs, including successful go-live delivery.
Cross-Functional Leadership:
Experience coordinating multiple workstreams, technical teams, and external implementation partners.
Execution & Risk Management:
Strong project execution skills, including managing timelines, budgets, resources, and implementation risks.
Stakeholder Management:
Ability to engage senior leadership, influence decisions, and drive alignment across business functions.

Your Responsibilities

Lead and oversee large-scale SAP transformation initiatives.
Manage program planning, execution, and delivery milestones.
Coordinate cross-functional teams and external implementation partners.
Oversee program budgets, resources, risks, and timelines.
Work with senior stakeholders to ensure alignment and accountability.
Support successful system deployment and organizational readiness.

jobs.title: Head of Enterprise Project & Change Management
jobs.description:
Synopsis of the Role

Reporting to the Chief Operations Officer (COO), the Head of Enterprise Project Management Office (EPMO) and Organizational Change Management Practice (OCM) provides enterprise-wide leadership and strategic oversight of Equifax Canada’s project and program portfolio, ensuring alignment with business priorities and strategic objectives.

This role partners closely with local and global leaders across Product, Technology, and Operations to drive execution excellence, strengthen portfolio governance, and accelerate business outcomes through effective project delivery and organizational change.

What You'll Do

Strategic Leadership, Governance & Portfolio Management

Enterprise Methodologies & Frameworks : Develop and implement enterprise-wide project management methodologies aligned with industry best practices (e.g., PMBOK, Agile, Lean), alongside robust Organizational Change Management (OCM) frameworks, tools, and standardized templates.
Portfolio Governance & Intake : Establish and manage a standardized project intake, business case evaluation, prioritization, and portfolio management framework aligned with strategic business outcomes.
Executive Reporting & Metrics : Develop, track, and report on key performance indicators (KPIs), scorecards, financial forecasts, and status summaries for senior leadership, steering committees, and C-Suite.
Continuous Improvement : Evaluate the ongoing effectiveness of current projects and change plans, driving continuous process enhancements and organizational learning

Project Intake, Planning & Execution

Scope & Capacity Planning : Collaborate with stakeholders to define project scope, deliverables, timelines, budgets, and portfolio resource capacity allocation.
Execution & Quality Oversight: Oversee projects execution, ensuring projects adhere to timelines, quality standards, budget limits, and formal scope change controls.
Risk Mitigation & Issue Resolution : Conduct risk assessments, implement mitigation plans, and provide direct guidance to project managers to remove operational roadblocks.
Kickoffs & Retrospectives : Lead project kickoffs and retrospectives to capture learnings and optimize future project execution.

Organizational Change Management & Adoption

Change Strategy : Drive end-to-end change management strategies for Canada across corporate, client, supplier, and employee programs. Define clear success metrics (e.g., speed and proficiency of adoption, employee feedback pulse surveys, project ROI, and reduction in rework), leverage structured frameworks such as Prosci/ADKAR or Kotter, and conduct targeted stakeholder engagement activities including impact assessments, executive sponsorship alignment, workshops, and feedback retrospective loops.
OCM Capability Building : Own the design, development, and delivery of enterprise OCM education programs, toolkits, and knowledge transfer across internal teams and external partners

Team Leadership & Development

Team Building & Mentorship : Build, inspire, and lead high-performing EPMO and OCM teams, fostering a collaborative, team-based environment.
Coaching & Performance Management : Establish clear performance expectations, conduct execution assessments, provide continuous feedback, and deliver professional development opportunities.

What Experience You Need

Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, Computer Science, Organizational Development, or a related field.
Professional Experience: 10+ years of experience in project management and/or change management, including 5+ years in leadership roles overseeing large-scale enterprise projects, multi-faceted change management, or program portfolios.
Executive Presence: Exceptional communication, conflict resolution, and stakeholder management skills with demonstrated gravitas to engage and influence C-Suite leadership.
Industry Experience: Financial Services or Fintech industry experience is required.
EPMO & OCM Scaling: Proven track record of establishing and scaling an enterprise PMO or OCM capability within a rapid-paced, high-growth environment
Technical Implementation Background: Hands-on experience with advanced technology implementations, enterprise consulting, cloud-based services, and PM tools such as Jira and MS Project.
Project Management Certifications: PMP (Project Management Professional) or PgMP (Program Management Professional) certification
Change Management Certifications: PROSCI or CCMP™ (Certified Change Management Professional) designation.

What Could Set You Apart

Advanced Education: Master’s degree (MBA or relevant advanced field) preferred.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
THE OPPORTUNITY

We have an amazing opportunity for a motivated operational Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to lead the organization’s strategic financial management, maintain stakeholder confidence and ensure the integrity of publicly filed financial statements. Reporting to the CEO, the CFO will provide timely and accurate financial information to support decisions concerning the organization’s short-, medium- and long-term direction. The CFO will provide advice and quarterly updates to the Audit Committee and Board of Directors, with additional updates as required.

The CFO will oversee accounting, budgeting, cash flow forecasting, liquidity management and financial systems across Nanalysis and its subsidiaries, including KPrime and RS2D. Working closely with operational leaders, the CFO will maintain effective internal financial controls, oversee consolidated financial reporting and ensure compliance with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).

THE ORGANIZATION

Nanalysis Scientific Corp. is a publicly traded company listed on the TSX Venture Exchange under the ticker symbol NSCI. The company develops and manufactures compact nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) instruments and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) technology for laboratory and industrial applications. Its products serve customers across pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, energy, chemicals, food science and materials, as well as government and university research laboratories worldwide.

Through RS2D, Nanalysis also offers magnetic resonance electronics and software for NMR and MRI applications. The group includes KPrime Technologies, which focuses on Canadian aviation and urban security markets, providing maintenance services for passenger screening and imaging equipment and offering security technology solutions.

Nanalysis operates across Scientific Equipment and Security Services. Its services business includes a long-term, $160 million contract with the Canadian Air Transport Security Authority (CATSA) to maintain security scanners at more than 80 Canadian airports.
For more information, please visit: www.nanalysis.com

PRIMARY DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES

Participate in strategic business, financial, and human resource planning, coordinating the preparation of budgets for the organization and commercial bank.
Lead an accounting/finance department of fifteen accounting and varied staff locally and internationally, and play a role in the overall administration and management of the organization.
Responsible for day-to-day financial operations including: operating cash-flow, management of the general ledger, banking, investments, payroll, accounts payable, accounts receivable, government reporting, and remitting.
Driving and overseeing the upgrading of accounting systems, the implementation of a new Microsoft-based ERP, that is suitable for the size and nature of Nanalysis and its subsidiaries.
Monitor revenue and expenditures as compared to budget and explain variances.
Provision of appropriate performance reports to the various departments within the organization, including subsidiaries.
Skills and experience in timely consolidation of quarterly financial statements required.
In addition to providing financial reports to CEO and the Board of Directors, the CFO will provide the management team with the financial and business process information they require to do their jobs optimally.
Preparation of quarterly F/S for external distribution along with meaningful MD&A.
Management of NCIB as directed by CEO and Board of Directors, and preparation of AIF and any regulatory documents required by the organization, as determined by the CEO and Board of Directors.
As authorized by the organization’s CEO and Board of Directors, endorse cheques, contracts, and other legal documents on behalf of the organization.
Liaise with external financial accountants and ensure production of annual audited financial statements.
Oversee the financial elements of strategic partnerships with outside entities.
Work with HR to maintain personnel files with employment information and salary verification; track vacation, leave, sick time, and overtime.
Review and challenge external invoices from accounting and legal firms as necessary.
Coordinate all payroll requirements, including new hires, terminations, and salary adjustments.
Administer employee benefits plan.
Maintain banking relations, including maintaining operating lines of credit that are required for business operations.
Liaise with legal advisors on financial matters.
Lead financial Due Diligence and ultimately integration for an aggressive multi-pronged acquisition strategy over the coming five years.
Other related work may be required.

QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum of 15 years of broad financial management experience, preferably with familiarity with public-company markets and M&A.
Experience managing finance (accounting, budgeting, control, reporting) for start-ups and/or small manufacturing organizations with international clients and multiple funding sources, including federal, provincial, and international governments, is preferred.
Professional accounting designation (CPA) with a related university degree.
Proficiency in accounting software (e.g. QuickBooks) and electronic payment systems.
Experience with ERP implementation and maintenance.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite as well as familiarity with Microsoft Dynamics.
Ability to undertake occasional business-related travel.

KEY COMPETENCIES

Excellent organizational, analytical, research, and time management skills.
Ability to work with an open and consultative communication style.
Capacity to work both independently and as a strong team player and leader, demonstrating flexibility, adaptability, timeliness, and responsiveness.
Ability to set priorities, to act decisively, and to exercise a high degree of initiative, diplomacy, and judgment on a wide range of issues, especially when dealing with confidential matters.
Superior skills in building and maintaining productive and supportive working relationships and dealing with others in a professional and respectful manner.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
THE OPPORTUNITY

We have an exceptional opportunity for a strategic, government-savvy finance leader to serve as Director of Finance and help shape the fiscal future of the Town of High Level. Reporting to the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO), the Director of Finance is responsible for the overall leadership and management of the Town’s financial operations. This includes overseeing strategic financial planning, accounting, revenue collection, and cash management, ensuring alignment with the Town’s adopted plans, policies, bylaws, regulations, and standards. In addition to fostering interdepartmental collaboration and ensuring compliance with all financial obligations as outlined in the Municipal Government Act (MGA), the Director supervises a team of four (4): a Financial Analyst, Accounts Payable and Receivable Clerk, Utilities and Tax Clerk, and Support Services Clerk.

THE ORGANIZATION

The Town of High Level is a vibrant northern community of approximately 4,000 residents, serving as the regional service and trading centre for a surrounding population of more than 30,000 people. Located in the northwest corner of Alberta, High Level is strategically positioned at the intersection of Highways 35 and 58, providing critical access to northern industries and communities.

High Level is recognized as a hub for healthcare, education, retail, construction, transportation, and resource development, offering a unique blend of professional challenge and community connection. Known for its breathtaking Northern Lights, endless summer days and access to pristine lakes, rivers and outdoor adventures, the Town is a gateway to exceptional northern living. Residents also enjoy a strong sense of community and rich Indigenous culture, with local festivals, rodeos, and family-oriented activities year-round.

Vision

High Level, an inclusive and vibrant community, with a strong and resilient economy that offers an active and healthy lifestyle.

Mission

We foster a thriving community that enhances our quality of life through sustainable planning, economic prosperity, and inclusion.

For more information, please visit their website: www.highlevel.ca

RESPONSIBILITIES

Plans, directs and coordinates the functions and workload within the Department and ensures that schedules, procedures and performance standards are developed and met.
Utilizes significant judgement, initiative and conceptual thinking in the planning, development and implementation of programs and policies affecting matters related to the scope of duties of this position.
Plans, directs and coordinates the preparation of annual and long-term operational and capital budgets. Provides direct oversight, control and implementation of approved budgets.
Responsible for the preparation of statements and reports on municipal financial affairs for CAO, Directors, Council and the public; includes financial reports on the status and variance of all operating and capital budgets.
Responsible for compiling and supplying information relating to the financial affairs of the municipality as required by Municipal Affairs.
Prepares all financial bylaws, resolutions and subsequent amendments relating to the revenues, expenditures, tax levies and other fiscal and operating matters within the scope of duties of this position. This includes, but is not limited to, bylaws related to the Financial Plan, fees & charges, user rates, tax rates, loan authorization and others.
Administers the provision and management of property insurance policies, claims and related activities.
Oversees the delivery of the Town’s support services, including audit, accounting, taxation, treasury functions, and the management of financial software systems.
Prepares year-end financial working papers, internal statements and municipal reporting forms for audit review and liaises with the Town auditors in connection with the financial audit.
Supports procurement and contract management processes to ensure fiscal responsibility.
Oversees the development and maintenance of the Town’s asset management plan, including strategies, policies and procedures.
Oversees the development of policies for Financial Services. Provides input to policies of other departments.
Provides advice to Town staff, including explanation and interpretation of bylaws, procedures and legislative requirements affecting the Financial Administration department related to the scope of duties of this position.
Responsible for the supervision and mentoring of finance staff including hiring, training, dismissal, appraisals and evaluations of Financial Services employees within approved personnel policies.
Directs, coordinates, and supervises subordinate staff activities and contract staff. Monitors their work performance and delegates work appropriately.
Prepares, or directs the preparation, of reports and makes recommendations to the Chief Administrative Officer on financial matters related to the scope of duties of the position.
Attends all Council meetings, Committee meetings, public hearings and public meetings as required and as directed by the Chief Administrative Officer.
Prepares reports and statistical summaries as necessary for review by the Chief Administrative Officer, Council or other bodies.
As a member of the Senior Management Team, supports and assists other senior managers and is respectful of colleagues' roles, responsibilities and perspectives.
May be required to assist the Town in providing emergency services. Duties assigned during an emergency may differ from regular duties.
Follows and ensures compliance with all policies, procedures, regulations and standards of the Town of High Level.

QUALIFICATIONS

Degree from a recognized post-secondary institution in Accounting, Finance, Business or Public Administration.
Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation.
Minimum of five (5) years of increasingly responsible, relevant experience in public sector finance (including supervisory experience), preferably in a local government setting, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Thorough and demonstrated knowledge of the principles and practices of public sector accounting standards (PSAS), internal control procedures, computerized financial applications, finance and fiscal planning, and budgetary, accounting and reporting systems.
Thorough and demonstrated knowledge of municipal legislation including the Municipal Government Act and other related regulations, policies and procedures.

KEY COMPETENCIES

Demonstrated knowledge of GAAP, Public Sector Accounting and Budget processes.
Demonstrated leadership skills.
Exceptional interpersonal, communication, presentation, public relations, problem-solving, investigative, decision-making, leadership and general management skills.
Effective written and verbal communication skills including the ability to prepare comprehensive, concise and clear reports and deliver oral presentations.
Ability to multi-task with strong attention to detail.
Results-oriented in a multi-faceted, fast-paced environment with changing priorities.
Knowledge of and demonstrated fiscal responsibility in support of budget preparation and control.
Ability to work effectively, independently and cooperatively in a team atmosphere.
Ability to exercise courtesy, tact, and diplomacy in the exchange of non-routine information with other employees, employees of private companies and members of the general public.
Exceptionally well organized and able to work effectively with minimal guidelines and supervision.
Ability to exercise sound judgement regarding confidential and sensitive information.
Proficiency in the use of Microsoft Office applications and extensive knowledge in computer systems relevant to municipal operations. Experience with Questica Budget and Diamond ERP Accounting Software is desired.

jobs.description:
Liftoff is a leading AI-powered performance marketing platform for the mobile app economy. Our end-to-end technology stack helps app marketers acquire and retain high-value users, while enabling publishers to maximize revenue across programmatic and direct demand.

Liftoff’s solutions, including Accelerate, Direct, Monetize, Intelligence, and Vungle Exchange, support over 6,600 mobile businesses across 74 countries in sectors such as gaming, social, finance, ecommerce, and entertainment. Founded in 2012 and headquartered in Redwood City, CA, Liftoff has a diverse, global presence.

We're seeking a Director to lead Deal Desk within Liftoff's Strategic Finance team that reports to the VP of Strategic Finance. This is a high-ownership role at the center of how Liftoff structures, approves, and manages commercial agreements, from standard arrangements to complex, non-standard deals with strategic advertising partners. As the ultimate DRI for revenue adjustments, deal economics, and the integrity of Liftoff's commercial commitments, you will partner closely with GTM, Finance, and senior leadership to set deal strategy, manage active deal performance, and ensure every commercial arrangement is entered into with a clear, defensible financial rationale. If you have deep comfort with ambiguity, strong independent judgment, exceptional attention to detail, and the ability to lead cross-functional processes with confidence, we want to hear from you!

Key Responsibilities:

Serve as DRI for all revenue adjustments in weekly reporting: own the underlying logic, file integrity, and formula soundness.
Maintain active reconciliation checks and ensure adjustments are accurate, complete, and explainable at any point in the week.
Work proactively with cross-functional partners throughout the week to incorporate new intel before weekly close.
Lead weekly alignment meetings with the FP&A team; own WoW variance explanation and post summaries to relevant stakeholders.
Own all deal types end-to-end ranging from standard structures to complex, unique, and customer-specific arrangements.
Maintain and enforce the Deal Desk approval matrix; lead a bi-annual Deal Desk Strategy Review with SLT.
Own the philosophy and commercial logic underlying how Liftoff approaches deal structures, including eligibility thresholds and deal parameters by customer segment.
For non-standard deals: lead upfront diligence including detailed financial modeling.
Lead weekly cross-functional reviews on active non-standard deals; make budget and commercial adjustment recommendations as needed.
Produce monthly performance updates on active deal programs for senior leadership, with clear variance analysis against original assumptions.
Monitor cash flows and financial commitments on structured deals; update models as actuals come in and flag deviations proactively.
Own and lead accrual review for all key Deal Desk items, including complex arrangements.
Hold a well-supported, defensible position on accrual levels, with the underlying data and logic ready to present in senior Finance forums.
This role includes direct management of a Senior Analyst, with responsibility for mentorship, prioritization, and maintaining high analytical standards across Deal Desk operations

Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field.
10+ years of experience in commercial finance, deal desk, revenue operations, or strategic finance; at least 5 years with direct ownership over deal structuring or commercial agreements.
Demonstrated ability to evaluate complex deal economics independently, build defensible financial models, and present clear recommendations to senior leadership.
Strong understanding of revenue recognition, accrual accounting, and the operational mechanics of commercial deal management.
Exceptional judgment: able to hold a position under commercial pressure while remaining collaborative and solutions-oriented.
Track record of true DRI ownership, including proactively surfacing risks, driving process, and escalating only when genuinely warranted.
Excellent communicator with experience presenting to CXO-level audiences.

Nice to have:

Ad tech, programmatic advertising, or mobile experience

If you're passionate about driving commercial excellence, managing complex deal structures, and partnering with leadership to ensure sound financial decision-making, we want to hear from you! Working at Liftoff is fast-paced, fun, and challenging, and we thrive on innovation. Come join the rocket ship and help shape the future of the mobile app ecosystem with us!

Location:

Liftoff follows a philosophy of "remote first, come together meaningfully" and allows employees to be based anywhere in Canada. We require that this role work during Pacific time zone; working from the Vancouver area is highly preferred.

Travel Expectations:
We offer several opportunities for in-person team gatherings, including but not limited to project meetings, regional meetups, and company-wide events. We expect our employees to attend these gatherings at least once per quarter. These gatherings provide essential opportunities for collaboration, communication, and team building.

Compensation:

Liftoff offers all employees a full compensation package that includes equity and health/vision/dental benefits associated with your country of residence. Base compensation will vary based on the candidate's location and experience.

The following is the OTE (base + bonus) salary range for Canada: CAD 185,000 - 230,000

new_jobs.description:
An opportunity for an experienced SAP leader to oversee complex enterprise technology transformation initiatives.

About the Company

Our client is an established organization undergoing significant technology and business transformation, with a focus on modernizing enterprise systems, improving operational efficiency, and supporting long-term growth.

Who You Are

You are an experienced SAP program leader with a proven track record of delivering large-scale ERP transformations. You combine strong technical knowledge with practical execution skills and are comfortable leading cross-functional teams, managing complex projects, and engaging senior stakeholders. You bring a collaborative yet decisive leadership style and understand what it takes to deliver successful enterprise implementations.

Your Impact

The SAP Program Director will provide leadership and oversight for a major enterprise systems transformation. The role involves coordinating multiple workstreams, managing implementation priorities, and ensuring effective delivery across business and technology functions. You will work closely with senior leadership, internal teams, and external partners to drive program execution and successful outcomes.

What Are We Looking For?

SAP Implementation Experience:
Demonstrated experience leading large-scale SAP implementations, including SAP S/4HANA.
Program Delivery Leadership:
Proven ability to manage complex, end-to-end ERP transformation programs, including successful go-live delivery.
Cross-Functional Leadership:
Experience coordinating multiple workstreams, technical teams, and external implementation partners.
Execution & Risk Management:
Strong project execution skills, including managing timelines, budgets, resources, and implementation risks.
Stakeholder Management:
Ability to engage senior leadership, influence decisions, and drive alignment across business functions.

Your Responsibilities

Lead and oversee large-scale SAP transformation initiatives.
Manage program planning, execution, and delivery milestones.
Coordinate cross-functional teams and external implementation partners.
Oversee program budgets, resources, risks, and timelines.
Work with senior stakeholders to ensure alignment and accountability.
Support successful system deployment and organizational readiness.
